column1: transport|A system for moving people or goods.|Public transport is available throughout the evening.
journey|Travel from one place to another.|Allow extra time for your journey during roadworks.
trip|A visit involving travel away from home.|Our day trip includes a guided museum visit.
route|The path taken to reach a destination.|The bus will follow a different route on Sunday.
destination|The place to which someone is travelling.|Check the destination before boarding the train.
departure|The act or time of leaving.|Passengers should arrive thirty minutes before departure.
arrival|The act or time of reaching a place.|Please notify reception of your expected arrival.
fare|The price paid for a journey.|The fare is cheaper outside the morning peak.
ticket|A document or electronic record allowing travel or entry.|Keep your ticket until you leave the station.
travel pass|A document allowing repeated travel or entry.|A weekly travel pass is cheaper for regular commuters.
platform|The area beside railway tracks where passengers wait.|The train to the coast leaves from platform four.
station|A place where trains or buses stop for passengers.|The station has step-free access from the main road.
bus stop|A place where buses pick up and drop off passengers.|The nearest bus stop is outside the library.
terminal|A building where passengers begin or end a journey.|The shuttle leaves from the international terminal.
airport|A place where aircraft arrive and depart.|The airport bus runs every thirty minutes.
port|A place where ships load and unload.|Ferry passengers must check in at the port office.
ferry|A boat that regularly carries people or vehicles across water.|The last ferry returns to the island at six.
tram|A passenger vehicle that runs on rails along streets.|Take the tram to the central market.
coach|A bus used mainly for longer journeys.|The coach has limited space for large luggage.
shuttle|A service making repeated trips between two places.|A free shuttle connects the hotel and the airport.
passenger|Someone travelling in a vehicle without operating it.|Each passenger may carry one small bag.
driver|Someone who operates a vehicle.|Ask the driver before bringing a bicycle aboard.
cyclist|Someone travelling by bicycle.|Every cyclist must dismount in the shopping area.
vehicle|A machine used to carry people or goods.|Do not leave valuables in your vehicle.
traffic|Vehicles moving on roads.|Heavy traffic may delay the airport shuttle.
delay|A period of waiting longer than expected.|There is a twenty-minute delay on this service.
closure|The temporary or permanent shutting of a route or facility.|The bridge closure will last until Monday.
crossing|A place where people can safely cross a road.|Use the marked crossing near the school.
roundabout|A circular road junction around a central island.|Take the second exit at the roundabout.
pavement|The area beside a road intended for walking.|Please keep bicycles off the narrow pavement.
lane|A marked strip of road for one line of vehicles.|Only buses may use this lane during peak hours.
cycle path|A route intended for people riding bicycles.|The cycle path connects the park and the station.
car park|An area where vehicles may be parked.|The visitor car park closes at midnight.
meter|A device that measures use or calculates a charge.|Pay at the parking meter before leaving your car.
fine|Money charged as a penalty for breaking a rule.|Parking on the pavement may result in a fine.
speed limit|The maximum legal speed on a road.|The speed limit is lower near the school.
seat belt|A safety strap that holds a passenger in a seat.|Fasten your seat belt before the vehicle moves.
helmet|A hard covering worn to protect the head.|A helmet is required for the guided cycling tour.
brake|A device that slows or stops a vehicle.|Test each brake before hiring the bicycle.
tyre|The rubber covering around a vehicle's wheel.|The mechanic will replace the worn tyre.
fuel|A substance used to produce energy for a vehicle.|Return the hire car with the same amount of fuel.
petrol|A liquid fuel used in some vehicle engines.|The nearest petrol station is two kilometres away.
charging point|A place where an electric vehicle can be recharged.|A charging point is available beside the visitor centre.
driving licence|An official document allowing someone to drive.|Bring your driving licence when collecting the hire car.
insurance|An arrangement providing financial protection against specified losses.|Check whether the rental price includes insurance.
rental|An arrangement to use something temporarily in return for payment.|The bicycle rental includes a lock and helmet.
hire|To pay to use something for a limited time.|You can hire a car from the airport desk.
return journey|Travel back to the place where a trip began.|The ticket includes the return journey.
single ticket|A ticket for travel in one direction.|A single ticket is enough if someone is driving you back.
return ticket|A ticket covering travel to a place and back.|Buy a return ticket before boarding the ferry.
peak|The busiest period for travel or demand.|Fares are higher during peak travel hours.
connection|A service that continues a journey after changing vehicles.|The late train may cause us to miss our connection.
boarding|Getting onto a vehicle for a journey.|Boarding begins fifteen minutes before the coach leaves.
check-in|The process of registering arrival for travel or accommodation.|Online check-in closes two hours before departure.
boarding pass|A document showing that a passenger may board a flight.|Keep your boarding pass ready at the gate.
passport|An official document used to identify a traveller abroad.|Your passport must be presented at check-in.
visa|Official permission to enter or stay in a country.|Check the visa requirements before booking your trip.
baggage|Bags and cases carried when travelling.|The baggage allowance is printed on your ticket.
luggage|Bags and cases taken on a journey.|Please store large luggage in the compartment below.
suitcase|A case used to carry clothes and belongings.|Label your suitcase with your contact details.
hand luggage|Small bags carried with a passenger inside a vehicle.|Keep essential documents in your hand luggage.
lost property|Items found after their owners have misplaced them.|Ask the lost property office about your umbrella.
map|A drawing showing places and routes.|Collect a walking map from the information desk.
direction|The way towards a place.|The sign shows the direction of the town centre.
distance|The space between two places.|The walking distance to the station is about a kilometre.
walking distance|A distance that can conveniently be covered on foot.|The hostel is within walking distance of the beach.
landmark|A noticeable feature used to identify a place.|The clock tower is a useful landmark near the station.
accommodation booking|An arrangement reserving a place to stay.|Please confirm your accommodation booking before travelling.
hostel|Low-cost accommodation often with shared rooms.|The hostel provides lockers for guests.
hotel|A business providing rooms for travellers.|The hotel reception is staffed throughout the night.
guest|Someone staying at accommodation or visiting another person.|Each guest receives a key card.
reception|The desk where visitors receive information or assistance.|Ask reception for a late check-out.
check-out|The process of leaving accommodation and settling charges.|Check-out is by ten in the morning.
tour|A journey around places of interest.|The walking tour lasts approximately ninety minutes.
guide|Someone who leads visitors and explains places.|Your guide will meet you outside the museum.
sightseeing|Visiting interesting places as a leisure activity.|The pass includes a sightseeing bus ride.
attraction|A place or activity that people visit for enjoyment.|The aquarium is a popular local attraction.
seasonal|Available or happening during a particular part of the year.|The seasonal bus service runs only in summer.
advance booking|Reserving a service before the time it is needed.|Advance booking is required for the evening tour.
fully booked|Having no places left to reserve.|The morning excursion is fully booked.
commuter|Someone who regularly travels between home and work.|The new timetable will help the early-morning commuter.
pedestrian|Someone travelling on foot.|The bridge has a separate path for pedestrian access.
congestion|A situation in which too many vehicles slow movement.|The new bus lane should reduce congestion.
diversion|An alternative route used when the usual one is closed.|Follow the diversion signs around the roadworks.
roadworks|Construction or repairs taking place on a road.|Roadworks will restrict access to the car park.
junction|A place where roads meet.|Turn left at the next junction.
parking permit|Permission to park in a restricted area.|Display your parking permit on the dashboard.
puncture|A small hole that allows air to escape from a tyre.|A puncture delayed our cycling trip.
breakdown|A failure that stops a vehicle or machine working.|Call the assistance number if you have a breakdown.
mileage|The distance a vehicle has travelled.|Write down the mileage when you collect the van.
off-peak|Outside the busiest travel periods.|An off-peak ticket cannot be used before nine.
interchange|A place where passengers can change transport services.|Change to the airport bus at the main interchange.
alight|To get off a bus, train or other vehicle.|Please alight at the stop opposite the museum.
customs|The official check of goods brought into a country.|Declare the goods when you reach customs.
immigration|The process or control of entering another country to stay.|Allow time for immigration checks after landing.
left luggage|A service that stores travellers' bags temporarily.|The station offers left luggage storage until eight.
itinerary|A plan of the places and times in a journey.|The tour company emailed our final itinerary.
excursion|A short organised journey for pleasure or learning.|The excursion includes a visit to the harbour.
reschedule|To arrange a different time for something.|You can reschedule the tour if the weather is unsuitable.
accessible transport|Transport that can be used by people with access needs.|Contact the centre to arrange accessible transport.
